back: A large-scale ecosystem identified by its dominant vegetation and its climate, such as savanna or tropical rainforest.
Climatic (temperature, rainfall, light), edaphic (soil), relief (altitude, slope, aspect) and biotic (competition, grazing, fire, people).
Biomass is a store of living material (kg per m²); net primary productivity is the rate of new growth (g per m² per year).
Emergent trees, canopy, understorey, shrub layer and ground layer.
Thick fire-resistant bark, deep taproots, leaf-drop in the dry season, grasses that regrow from ground-level buds, and migration of grazers.
Succulents store water; spines and small or waxy leaves reduce loss; wide shallow roots; ephemerals germinate only after rain.

front: Typical NPP of rainforest and desert
back: Tropical rainforest about 2 200 g per m² per year; hot desert about 90 g per m² per year (textbook values, rounded).
Temperature falls about 6.5 °C per 1 000 m, shortening the growing season and changing the plant types.
Around 15–30° from the equator, where air sinks and rainfall is below about 250 mm.
